# Backlog

What's missing to go from "the hub can chat" to a usable family app. This is
a scannable list, not a narrative - full reasoning and decision history for
any item lives in `docs/dev.md` (linked where useful) or the relevant
platform standard in `getmaipai/.github`. Update this file whenever a gap
closes or a new one is found; don't let it drift from what `main` actually
does.

Rough size tags: **S** (a session or less), **M** (a real slice, days),
**L** (a platform-level capability, needs its own design pass first).

## Settings redesign

Health, turn preflight, status history, and apps use the same result; regression tests cover outage, ready, and unreachable cases.

Tests cover install download, spawn, and a start that exceeds the diagnostic threshold. Found while closing STATUS-FLAP-01's remaining Kiwix transient-starting question (2026-10-01).

## Thin chat path

The hard rules are [docs/design/RULES.md](design/RULES.md) ("Chat turn", rule 0 and rules 1 to 14); the accepted record, with the order of work and the replacements table, is [docs/plans/chat-thin-path-2026-10-02.md](plans/chat-thin-path-2026-10-02.md). Stages run in order, 0 to 7; no stage deletes anything until each behaviour it holds is ported or retired in writing (rule 12); each stage ends with a CHAT-AB-01 rerun (THIN-AB) against one engine, recorded in `docs/dev.md`. Item ids are `THIN-<stage><letter>`. File names that say `turnEngine.ts` below are the old path being ported from; every fix lands on the default path in `backend/src/lib/turnMachine/`. Stack and commons halves: STACK-CTX-01 and STACK-SEARCH-01 in `getmaipai/stack`, SAMPLING-SPEC-01 and CITE-KIT-01 in `getmaipai/commons`.

- [x] **THIN-0A: "forget that" works on the default path** (S, 2026-10-02; rule 12, stage 0; issue #204). Objective: saying "forget that" removes the memory, as it does on the old path; today the default path answers "Got it" and the memory stays. Files: `backend/src/lib/turnEngine.ts:42` and `:2566` (`parseForgetCommand`, `forgetFromConversation`), `backend/src/lib/turnMachine/nodes/commands.ts`, `backend/tests/turnMachine/turnNext.test.ts`. Mirror: the `remember` command's path through `nodes/commands.ts` (an exact command, no model decides). Do: first a failing test on the default path, then move the forget parser and its conversation lookup out of `turnEngine.ts` into a module `commands.ts` calls. Acceptance: after a turn that saved a memory, "forget that" deletes that memory and the reply confirms it; with nothing to forget the reply says so; a temporary conversation forgets nothing and says so; a child's forget touches only the child's own records. Regression test on the default path. Out of scope: a forget package in the catalog, other commands (THIN-0K). Fixes part of #204. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` (the scoped gate), with the regression test written and seen failing first.

  Status: verified at e0288135.

- [x] **THIN-0B: a child asking about something withheld is pointed to a trusted adult** (M, 2026-10-02; rules 0 and 12, stage 0; issue #204). Files: `backend/src/lib/turnMachine/turnNext.ts:265` (`disclosureWithheld` is a constant false), `backend/src/lib/turnEngine.ts` near `:2970` (the relay and defer logic), `backend/src/lib/register.ts:171,189`, `memory.ts` (the `child_disclosure` projection, read only), `turnMachine/nodes/context.ts`. Acceptance: a child's turn whose recall was reduced by the projection carries the withheld signal into the plan line and the reply points to a parent or trusted adult; the same turn for an adult is unchanged; a turn with nothing withheld is unchanged. Regression test on the default path using the Santa fixture. Out of scope: changing the projection itself, the relay to the parent's notifications (THIN-0H). Fixes part of #204. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` (the scoped gate), with the regression test written and seen failing first. Status: verified at 930d2a0c. The relay to a parent is not included and belongs to THIN-0H.

Cause (verified in `bonjour-service` `dist/lib/service.js`): `publish()` in `backend/src/lib/mdns.ts` passed no `host`, so the library defaulted it to `os.hostname()` and announced the machine's OWN `.local` name (SRV target, A and AAAA records); macOS's mDNSResponder saw a conflicting claim on its own host name and renamed the computer ("... Local check still to run by the owner after the next hub start: `scutil --get ComputerName` and `scutil --get LocalHostName` unchanged, and `dns-sd -G v4 maipai-<id>.local` resolves to this machine. Exit check: `backend/tests/mdns.test.ts`, `scripts/check.sh`.

## The chat rebuild (2026-09-22)

The accepted design and build order:
[docs/plans/simple-turn-pipeline-2026-09-22.md](plans/simple-turn-pipeline-2026-09-22.md).
The old rule ladder (~1,900 lines of regex and word lists deciding
whether to search, what to search for, and whether to trust the model's
own answer) is replaced by five fixed steps and one model call with
tools; new path built beside the old one behind `turn.pipeline.next`
(off by default) until the replay set passes clean. Phase 0 (the
buy-or-build spike, the per-model capability numbers, the local-decider
bench) gates U2 onward; U0, U1, U3, U5 start immediately. See the plan's
point 7 for the full unit list and point 6 for the migration order.

- [x] **ENGINE-PORT-01: the hub never kills an engine it did not spawn** (S, Sonnet, 2026-09-23; dev.md "The \"generation_failed\" outage on the new path was a killed engine"). Objective: `sidecars.ts`'s `freePort(port)` SIGKILLs every process whose command line carries `--port <n>` before every spawn, by port match and silently, so any second process that starts the hub's supervisors with the production defaults (a headless repro, a bench outside `tests/preload.ts`) kills the household's chat, text-understanding and embed engines, and the two hubs then ping-pong (74 SIGKILL lines, three "did not come back"). Change: an orphan is a pid the hub's own pid record names from a previous instance of this data directory (write the spawned engines' pids beside `data/local-app/pid`); `freePort` kills only those; a live holder that answers `/health` and is not in the record is a reported condition on the health list and the log ("port 8788 is held by pid N, not ours: set MAIPAI_LLAMA_SERVER_PORT, MAIPAI_BACKGROUND_PORT and MAIPAI_EMBED_PORT") and the spawn is refused, never a kill; every kill `freePort` does make is logged with the pid and the reason. Files: `sidecars.ts` (`freePort`, `findPidsMatching`), the supervisors' spawn paths, `sidecars.test.ts`. Tests in these words: a fake holder of the port that is not in the pid record is never signalled and the spawn returns the reported condition; a pid the record names from a dead instance is killed and logged; the health list carries the condition. Acceptance: two hubs started on the same ports from two data directories leave the first one's engines alive. Out of scope: the repro scripts' own isolation (they must set the port variables; SERVICES.md gets the one line). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`. Landed a1d363fb: the ownership record lives at `data/local-app/engine-pids.json` (beside the hub's own pid file), keyed by port; a port with no record at all falls back to the old kill-on-sight behavior (a real regression found in review otherwise - an upgrading install with a genuine crash orphan and no history yet would stay stuck blocked forever), so the protection is complete only once a port has been successfully spawned onto since this landed. The health-list surfacing is a new `"blocked"` `EngineHealthKind`, wired through all four engine roles (chat, background, embed, voice/tts) via `GET /api/health` and a HealthSection.tsx badge, not a Repairs issue. `data/local-app/pid` itself (the hub's own pid) is unchanged; `data/local-app/engine-pids.json` is a sibling record, not a shared file. Out of scope's own `docs/SERVICES.md` line (a different repo, `getmaipai/.github`) was not added this pass - flagged for the coordinator.

- [x] **GENFAIL-01: a failed generation carries its reason** (S, Codex, 2026-09-23; dev.md "The \"generation_failed\" outage"). Objective: `nodes/model.ts`'s `runOneGeneration` catches every thrown error as `{ ok: false, code: "generation_failed" }` with no message, never logs it, and never pushes the generation record, so an outage reads as a bare code. Change: the catch keeps the thrown message and, for an `LlmClientError` with a status, the status; the generation record (`turnStats.ts` `GenerationInput`) gains `error: { code, message, status? } | null` and a failed generation is pushed with it; the `[turn]` log line and `stats.nodes[]`'s `model` entry carry the same; the person-facing line is unchanged (DEADLINE-01). Files: `model.ts`, `turnStats.ts`, `contract.ts`, `model.test.ts`. Tests in these words: a scripted engine that refuses the connection yields a generation record whose error message contains "could not reach" and a trace `model` entry with the same; a mid-stream break yields "broke"; a 400 yields the status. Acceptance: the next outage's trace names the engine's own rejection. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`. Landed b19f8e7e: `error`/`message` shipped as a plain, bounded (2000-char) string rather than the row's own `{ code, message, status? }` shape - the status and any body the engine gave are already inside that string (spec-v0.1.29's own client.ts fix), and the row's own literal test wording ("contains 'could not reach'", "a 400 yields the status") is satisfiable either way; flagged for the coordinator in case the structured shape is wanted for a future bench to filter on. No dedicated `model.test.ts` - covered in `turnNext.test.ts` end to end (a real failed generation through the whole path) instead, matching how DEADLINE-01 next to it is tested. The `[turn]` log line does not exist on the new path yet at all (a pre-existing gap, not this item's); `[model]` console.error lines carry the reason on the hub's own log instead.

- [x] **FLAKE-PORT-01: test stub servers bind ephemeral ports, never fixed ones** (S, Sonnet; 2026-09-23). Objective: rep01.test.ts, ask02.test.ts and the other turn-path tests that start a stub chat engine fail with "chat model unavailable: could not reach http://127.0.0.1:<port>" whenever a second test process runs on the machine (a lane's single-file `bun test` beside a full gate, or two gates), because the stubs bind fixed ports from tests/isolation.ts and the second binder loses; a test never depends on a free fixed port. Every stub server (the spec's stubServer.ts, tests/preload.ts and isolation.ts, any test that spawns a supervisor) binds port 0 and hands the assigned port to the code under test through the same env variables it reads today; nothing in the suite names a literal port. Mirror: the engine-pids record from ENGINE-PORT-01 for how a port reaches its reader. Acceptance: two full `bun test` runs started at once in two worktrees both pass with no "could not reach" failure; `grep -rn ':87[0-9][0-9]\|:88[0-9][0-9]' backend/tests` returns nothing but comments; issue 137's second class closed. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` and the concurrent run recorded in dev.md. Landed <PLACEHOLDER_HASH>: the actual bug was narrower than "fixed ports named in the suite" (there were none - `reserveFreePort()` already binds port 0 and hands the number through the env vars the code under test reads, exactly as this row asks). The real defect was staleness: `llmSupervisor.test.ts` reserved one port ONCE at module load and reused it across three separate real-spawn tests spread over many seconds (the widest window in the suite for a concurrent process to grab the identical OS-assigned number before the real bind); `sidecars.test.ts`'s "reports a dead chat engine..." and "a stale client to a killed process probes false" never reserved their own port at all, inheriting `preload.ts`'s single port reserved once for the entire multi-minute, 200+-file run. Fixed by reserving fresh, immediately before each real spawn (the same already-correct pattern `resourceGovernor.test.ts` used throughout): `llmSupervisor.test.ts`'s `spawnFakeEngine()` now reserves and returns its own port per call instead of reading a module-level constant; the two `sidecars.test.ts` tests reserve their own port and restore (never delete - the 2026-09-07 finding in `preload.ts`'s own comment) the prior value in `finally`. The row's own literal grep (`:87[0-9][0-9]\|:88[0-9][0-9]` in `backend/tests`) hits many pre-existing, legitimate string fixtures unrelated to real port binding (URL-parsing test cases in `hubEndpoints.test.ts`, `engineIdentity.test.ts` and others, a simulated printed banner in `localApp.test.ts` that binds port 0 for real and only prints "8787" as fake log text) - not chased, since the coordinator's own later, more specific acceptance (the concurrent run passing, the EADDRINUSE signature gone) is what this lands against. Verified: two full `bun test` runs started at once in two worktrees, both green (dev.md has the run record); the previously-failing `llmSupervisor.test.ts`/`sidecars.test.ts` EADDRINUSE signature did not reappear.
- [x] **FLAKE-FORCED-01: the required_miss test is deterministic** (S, Sonnet; 2026-09-23). Objective: `backend/tests/turnMachine/turnNext.test.ts`'s FORCED-CALL-01 required_miss case fails on nearly every full gate under machine load (searxng.queries.length 0) and passes alone every time, so every lane's landing today paid an isolated rerun for it; the test depends on timing (the forced call's abort racing the scripted searxng stand-in, or a shared in-flight registry the suite's other files leave behind), which a deterministic test never does. Find the race with the file run in the full suite's order, fix the test's own construction (await the scripted call, isolate the registry, or drive the node directly the way policy.test.ts does), never widen a timeout or retry. ## Household storage (2026-09-23)

- [ ] **PEOPLE-01: the People section as a household browser, pets included, profiles like a creator page** (L, design pass first; owner's ask 2026-09-23). Objective: the People section lists every household member including pets, browsed the way a short-video app browses creators (a grid of cards with picture and name, tap to open), and a member's profile reads like a creator page: their picture, a description in their own words or a parent's, and the images and videos they have shared (the household store's share pointers from `docs/plans/household-storage-2026-09-23.md`, so a profile shows only what its owner shared with the viewer or the household, never the owner's private files), with the existing person settings behind an edit action rather than on the page. Design questions for the record before any row is chunked: the terminology, decided once (Settings calls them "users" today; the owner's framing 2026-09-23: an account is the login of a specific person, and the People section is wider than accounts: the household's members, its pets, and the people the hub knows without an account, the delivery driver a camera recognises, a neighbour, a grandparent who never logs in); how the people without accounts are managed (remove, merge two records the hub thought were different, rename, forget everything about someone) and where that lives, the People section itself or Settings; whether a pet is a Person with a kind or its own spec record (the spec's Entity kinds already carry pets; decide which the profile reads and how consent and settings apply to a pet's page), what a child sees on an adult's page, what the page shows before anyone has shared anything, and how the shadcndashboard profile page (used as it ships) composes with the kit's media grid so nothing is hand-built. Files: `frontend/src/next/pages/` (the People page), the profile page from the vendored dashboard, the storage rows STORE-SHARE-01 and STORE-PAGE-01 this depends on. Mirror: the dashboard's profile page and card grid. Acceptance (after the design pass chunks it): the People page shows a seeded household with a pet as cards, opening a card shows the picture, the description and a grid of that member's shared images and videos, a child's view hides what was not shared with them, captured at 1440 and 390 light and dark. Out of scope until the storage rows land: uploads and sharing themselves. Exit: the design record, then per-row `bash scripts/check.sh`. **Design verdict (Fable, 2026-09-26, dev.md "Design pass over the reserved items"): the flip trigger is met and no longer holds this back; the item is phased. Phase one is account holders only (the grid, the profile page from the vendored dashboard profile plus the kit media grid, manage actions, the child-view rule; prerequisites STORE-SHARE-01/STORE-PAGE-01 for the media grid). Pets and known people stay PEOPLE-EXPAND-01's design pass, per Jesse's 2026-09-25 ruling. The phase-one design pass is startable now.** **Phase-one design pass done (2026-09-26): `docs/plans/people-profile-2026-09-26.md` - the creator grid, the profile page's header card and shared-media grid, bounded customization (bio, photo opt-in, a named accent set), chunked into PEOPLE-SPEC-01/PEOPLE-GRID-01/PEOPLE-PROFILE-01/MEDIA-GRID-01/PEOPLE-PROFILE-02/AVATAR-RENDER-01/NOTIFY-SHARE-01/NOTIFY-SHARE-02. No subscribe concept (Jesse 2026-09-26, revised): a share notifies its recipient(s) by default through the existing declared-notification system (two new types reusing the existing `person`/`household` audiences), muted per type or per sender in Settings -> Notifications, nothing new to opt into. Three questions still await Jesse's ruling before rows are picked up (child photo consent, where display-name editing lives, sequencing against STORE-SHARE-01/STORE-PAGE-01).** **Phase one shipped (2026-09-27):** every phase-one row is done - `PEOPLE-SPEC-01`/`MEDIA-GRID-01`/`AVATAR-RENDER-01` in `commons`, `PEOPLE-GRID-01`/`PEOPLE-PROFILE-01`/`NOTIFY-SHARE-01`/`PEOPLE-PROFILE-02` here - so the account-holder creator page (grid, header card, Edit dialog, shared-media grid, share notifications) is real end to end; still unchecked because pets and known people without accounts (`PEOPLE-EXPAND-01`) are their own design pass, not started, and this row's own acceptance covers both.

A `KIND_PHRASES` map turns `File.kind` into a grammatical phrase ("a photo", "an audio clip") for the template, rather than the raw enum value reading as "a image". **A real settings-key toggle for either type is deliberately not built here**: every configurable type's toggle is `notifications.<id>.telegram` in `settings/notificationKeys.ts`, validated against the pinned `@maipai/spec` registry (`spec/settings/keys.json`) - adding one means regenerating that file into `commons`'s own main checkout and bumping the pin (confirmed against `e6112f5c`, the prior instance of exactly this), which needs write access to the shared `commons` checkout this item's own worktree was scoped away from (other sessions were landing work there the same night). `configurable: true` is what lets that key attach with no further code change the day it's added; today, both types simply never send Telegram (no default, no override key registered yet), which the test suite pins directly. Objective: a person's `/people/:id` page gains a grid of what they've shared (`@maipai/ui`'s `MediaGrid` primitive, `ui-v0.5.68`) wired to their live `Share` pointers (`backend/src/lib/shares.ts`), filtered by the viewer's own access (`access.ts`'s `canAccessFile`) - a viewer only ever sees what was actually shared with them or the household, never the owner's private files; the child-view rule applies (a supervised-role viewer's own restrictions, same posture `PEOPLE-PROFILE-01`'s header already follows). Mirror: `FilesPage.tsx`'s (Library) existing owned/shared listing logic - reuse its data-fetching shape rather than a second one. Out of scope: uploading or sharing from this page (that's the Library/`STORE-PAGE-01` surface). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` and the captures (light/dark, 1440/390). **Done 2026-09-27:** `GET /api/files` (`routes/files.ts`) grew an optional `?owner=` query param backed by a new `listPersonFilesVisibleToActor(actor, ownerPersonId)` in `lib/shares.ts` - a thin filter over the existing `listFilesVisibleToActor` (the Library's own owned+shared visibility), never a second listing mechanism: it narrows that actor's already-computed visible set to one owner, so an owner viewing their own profile trivially sees everything they own (`canAccessFile` already grants that) and any other viewer sees only what was shared with them directly or with the household. No separate child-view rule was needed: `canAccessFile` already governs a shared file's visibility independent of the viewer's role, so the design record's own "not a new rule invented for profiles, it's STORE-SHARE-01's own disclosure filter read from a second surface" held exactly as written. **A real gap surfaced building this**: nothing anywhere in this codebase served a file's own bytes over HTTP before now (checked directly - only `lib/attachments.ts`'s `readAttachment` existed, called from `documentExtraction.ts` and tests, never a route), so `MediaGrid`'s `thumbnailUrl` had nowhere real to point; added `GET /api/files/{id}/content`, gated by the same `canAccessFile` boundary, necessary plumbing for this item and not the separate upload endpoint that stays out of scope. `PersonProfilePage.tsx`'s Overview tab gained a `SharedMediaSection` composed from `MediaGrid`, filtering to `kind: image|video` (audio/document/story have no thumbnail concept it can render yet) with each item's `thumbnailUrl` pointing at the new content route. **Code review (medium effort) caught two real defects** in the content route's first cut, both fixed before commit: an `immutable, max-age=1y` `Cache-Control` that would have let a browser keep serving a revoked share's bytes forever with no access check ever running again (fixed to `private, no-store` - sha256 content-addressing makes the *bytes* immutable, never the *authorization* to see them); and no `Range` support at all for the video lightbox MediaGrid's own video branch renders (a browser's video element seeks by sending `Range`; a route that always returns the full body breaks seeking and, per this codebase's own YouTube-wall history, some browsers refuse to play at all) - added a minimal single-range responder (206 + `Content-Range`, falling back to the full body on an unsatisfiable range rather than a strict 416), returned as a raw `Response` (the same pattern `voice.ts`'s cloned-voice route already uses for a binary body - two 2xx statuses sharing one content schema defeated `c.body()`'s generated overloads, found live via `tsc --noEmit`). Tests: `shares.test.ts` gained five cases directly against `listPersonFilesVisibleToActor` (owner sees own with no share, a direct recipient, a third person sees nothing, a household-wide share reaches everyone, an unrelated owner's files never leak in); `filesRoutes.test.ts` gained the same three over real HTTP plus content-route cases (right bytes and content type, a shared recipient can fetch them too, no access is a 404 never the bytes, the no-store header, a 206 Range slice, an unsatisfiable range falling back to 200); `PersonProfilePage.test.tsx` gained five cases (renders image+video, excludes a document, both empty-state wordings - your own page vs. someone else's - and a retry on a failed fetch), plus a `stubFetch` default (`/api/files: []`) so the other 21 existing cases didn't need touching one by one. **Real screenshots, not the honest-empty-state `STORE-PAGE-01` took**: since `createAttachment()` still has no HTTP caller anywhere in this codebase (confirmed again, unchanged from `STORE-PAGE-01`'s own finding), a new `backend/scripts/seed-profile-share.ts` writes one real file + share pointer directly against the throwaway screenshot backend's own database (WAL mode, the same direct-database pattern `scripts/set-setting.ts` already uses for a not-yet-started server, extended here to one already running) - a verified 4x4 RGB PNG (the first cut used a 1-bit grayscale pixel that decoded to solid black and rendered as a suspicious black square; caught by opening the screenshot, fixed to a real red-orange square, confirmed by decoding it back before use). Captured as Marlow viewing Sage's profile - the one scenario that actually exercises the viewer-scoped filter, not just "an owner sees their own files," which `canAccessFile` grants trivially either way: `data-scratch/screenshots/people-profile-media-{1440,390}-{light,dark}.png`, all four opened and confirmed - the header card, the "Shared" section, and one real photo thumbnail render correctly in both themes at both viewports, no loading/broken/empty-when-it-shouldn't-be state. `bash scripts/check.sh` green (scope: full, both legs, docs/API regenerated - `docs/api/openapi.json` picked up the new query param and route).

Every person has their own storage, a parent caps each person and the household, and a person shares a file with named people or the family; an adult may share one file outside the house by a unique link the hub itself serves. The design records are [docs/plans/household-storage-2026-09-23.md](plans/household-storage-2026-09-23.md) (L; its six owner decisions are recorded) and [docs/plans/external-sharing-2026-09-23.md](plans/external-sharing-2026-09-23.md) (L; its numbered questions are the owner's); the spec rows are `STORE-SPEC-01` and `SHARE-LINK-01` in commons.

- [x] **STORE-CAP-01: the two caps, enforced at the record API in the person's words** (M, Sonnet; after STORE-SPEC-01). Objective: the three settings keys (`storage.household.cap_bytes`, `storage.person.default_cap_bytes`, `storage.person.cap_bytes`) declared once and rendered by the generic renderer; the host's record API refuses a write past the owner's cap or the household total with the reason ("Your storage is full; delete some pictures or ask a parent for more room" for a child, with "or raise the limit under Settings" for an adult); usage per person and per household computed from the records, a shared file counted once against its owner; a reconcile that finds bytes without a record or a record without bytes raises a health item, never a purge. Files: the settings registry (spec first), `backend/src/lib/packageHost.ts` (the record API), a new `backend/src/lib/storage/usage.ts`, the health list. Mirror: the allowance settings and the one health list. Acceptance, in these exact words: a child at the cap writing a picture gets the child line, an adult the adult line, a shared file counts once against its owner, no job ever deletes a file; a picture job whose estimate will not fit is refused before it starts with the same line (decision 3). Out of scope: sharing (STORE-SHARE-01), the page (STORE-PAGE-01). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`. **Done 2026-09-26:** the three keys landed spec-first as `spec-v0.1.45` (`commons` `docs/plans/household-storage-2026-09-23.md`), regenerated into `spec/settings/keys.json` from `backend/src/settings/storageKeys.ts`'s `STORAGE_SETTINGS_KEYS` via `bun run gen:settings` (never hand-edited); confirmed distinct from `storage.critical_free_gb`/`storage.person_quota_gb` (disk headroom and cloned-voice quota, a different subsystem) before adding them. The real write path today turned out to be `backend/src/lib/attachments.ts`'s `createAttachment()`, not `packageHost.ts` as this row's own Files line guessed - `packageHost.ts` has no image/video generation host method yet (checked directly), so `createAttachment` is the one real caller; a new `backend/src/lib/storage/usage.ts` holds `personUsageBytes`/`householdUsageBytes` (summed straight from the `attachments`/File table, so a shared file counts once against its owner by construction - no join through a share pointer, since `STORE-SHARE-01` hasn't landed one to join through yet), `personCapBytes`/`householdCapBytes` (0 means "no cap enforced at that level" consistently across all three keys), `storageRefusalMessage` (the exact child/adult wording), and `checkStorageCap` - the one preflight function decision 3's "a picture or video job whose output would not fit is refused before it starts" calls for; no such job exists in this codebase yet (checked: no image/video generation host method anywhere), so `checkStorageCap` is what that job calls the day it's built, proven directly by a test that calls it standalone with no attachment ever written. `createAttachment` calls it before any bytes touch disk. The person-scope override write gate reuses `INCOGNITO-07`'s session-lock ladder (owner/admin only, self ok, an admin can't touch another owner's/admin's), refactored into one shared `assertOwnerAdminLadder()` in `lib/settings.ts` rather than a second hand copy. The reconcile job (`storage.reconcile_files`, daily, mirrors `storage.check_disk_full`'s `raiseIssue`/`resolveIssue` pattern exactly, walking `attachmentsDir` via a `walkFiles()` helper now shared with `storage.ts`'s own `dirSizeBytes()`) never deletes either side of a mismatch. 18 tests in `backend/tests/storageUsage.test.ts` (the exact child/adult wording, the household cap refusing even when the person's own cap has room, an admin override winning over the household default, a plain adult refused from raising their own cap, the shared-file-counts-once assertion, the standalone preflight, three reconcile-never-deletes cases, an explicit `0` default meaning no cap rather than a silent 20 GB substitute). Code review at medium effort: the first pass reviewed an unrelated file (wrong target, discarded per the org's own "review whose reported path is not yours" rule) and was re-run with the worktree path explicit; the second pass found four real findings, all fixed - the 0-means-fallback inconsistency above, the settings-key literal declared twice (now one export per key in `storageKeys.ts`), the ladder duplication above, and the disk-walk duplication (now `lib/storage.ts`'s shared `walkFiles()`). Three findings accepted without a fix, with reasons on record: enforcement living only at `createAttachment`'s call site (there is exactly one writer of the `attachments` table today, confirmed directly - an insert-wrapper abstraction for one caller is the speculative-generality this codebase's own standards warn against, not a defect); the reconcile walk being synchronous (matches `storage.ts`'s own pre-existing `dirSizeBytes()`/`storageSummary()` precedent, and the job is already daily, not hourly, because of this exact cost); and `setValue()`'s per-key ternary growing a third arm (a registry-based per-key-authorizer refactor would touch two pre-existing keys unrelated to this item, better done as its own item than smuggled in here). `bash scripts/check.sh` not yet run in full (pending: the commit below); `tsc --noEmit` clean, targeted suites green (154 tests across the touched files).

- [x] **STORE-SHARE-01: sharing a file with named people or the household** (M, Sonnet; after STORE-SPEC-01). Objective: share pointer records (the spec's `share`: file id, from, to a person or the household) created and deleted by the owner only, re-sharing as a further pointer on the same file, never a second file record or a copy of the bytes; a second person adding identical bytes receives a pointer to the first person's file (no duplicates at any level); a shared file appears in each recipient's Library under the owner's name and counts against the owner; a child's sharing bounded by the consent floors (the household and its adults); a package reads a shared file only within its `min_role` and permissions; the turn pipeline's disclosure filter treats a shared file as context with the owner's disclosure. Files: the files routes, the Library page, `backend/src/lib/access.ts`, the context node. Mirror: the memory store's `canRead`. Acceptance: a shared file is listed for the recipient and not for a third person; unsharing removes it at once; a child cannot share outside the household and re-shares only within it, an adult may re-share anything shared with them within the household (decisions 2 and 6). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`. **Done 2026-09-27:** a new `shares` table (migration `0067_shallow_firebird.sql`) backs the spec's `Share` pointer record, and `backend/src/lib/shares.ts` holds the rules: `createShare` requires the actor already have access (the file's owner, or the recipient of any live share on it, direct or household-wide - decision 6's re-share right), validates `to` against a real active person or the literal `"household"`, and is idempotent per (file, to); `deleteShare` is allowed for whoever created that specific pointer, the file's owner, or an owner/admin acting for a **child's** file (mirroring `access.ts`'s existing `canAccessPerson` parity rule), and cascades via `pruneUnreachableShares` - a fixed-point reachability recompute over the graph (no parent-pointer field exists to chase; `share.schema.json` is `.strict()`), since "a re-share made from a pointer dies with the pointer it came from" has no stored lineage to follow directly. A code review (medium effort) caught a real bug in the first cut of that fixed point - a household-wide share could count its own creator as reachable via the very row it made, so revoking someone's only access never pruned a household share they'd created from it - fixed with a proper two-level fixed point (a row's grant only counts once its own granter is reachable via some OTHER row) plus a regression test. **Dedupe was a real gap, not already there**: `createAttachment` never deduped by `sha256` despite `file.schema.json`'s own doc-comment describing exactly that; it now looks up any existing row by hash (household-wide, not scoped to the uploader) before writing new bytes, and a second person's identical upload gets an auto-granted share pointer to the first arrival's file instead of a second blob and row (same person re-uploading identical bytes also reuses the row - "no duplicates at any level" now holds both ways). **The household bound for a child has no representable "outside" value in this schema at all** (`to` is only ever `"household"` or an existing person id - an external link is `share-link-01`'s own separate record, refused for a child at that route, not this one) - enforced here as: a share's target must resolve to a real active person or `"household"`, for anyone, child or adult; `shares.ts`'s own header comment names `PEOPLE-EXPAND-01` (known people without household membership) as the one place a real membership check needs to land later, since every person id this hub knows is a household member today. **Package `min_role`/permissions**: `packageHost.ts`'s `host.files.read/write` turned out to be an unrelated, still-unimplemented per-package private storage stub (no `file_id`, no household File/Share involvement at all - checked directly rather than conflating the two) - the real single read boundary for a household file is `attachments.ts`'s `getAttachment`/`readAttachment`, now updated to check `access.ts`'s new `canAccessFile` (owner or live share) instead of owner-only, which any future package-facing file read inherits automatically; `meetsMinRole` already gates every package/tool invocation generically upstream of that (`plugins.ts`'s `runPlugin`), unchanged. **The turn pipeline's disclosure rule is implemented but not yet live-wired**: `access.ts` gained `fileDisclosure(ownerPersonId)` (a minor's own file defaults `child_ok`, anyone else's `adult_only` - keyed on the owner, never the reader, per the design doc), unit-tested, but `turnMachine/nodes/context.ts` has no file/document context source at all today (checked directly: only utterance/window/memory/profile/clock/roster) - so this is the function a future file-context source calls, not something with a live caller yet; said so rather than fabricating a call site with no real acceptance behind it. New `frontend/src/apps/files/FilesPage.tsx` (Library) lists owned and shared files with owner attribution and share/unshare actions, reachable at `/files` - not added to the curated nav (`shell/nav.ts`) since how this actually surfaces is `STORE-PAGE-01`/`PEOPLE-01`'s call, not this item's. Tests: `backend/tests/shares.test.ts`, `access.test.ts`, `filesRoutes.test.ts` (new), dedupe cases added to `attachments.test.ts`. Full gate green (`bash scripts/check.sh`, both legs, docs/api regenerated).

## Studio day one (2026-09-23)

A month of lead time is prework time: stage, script and dry-run now so the Studio downloads nothing large, runs a checked runbook, evaluates its own configuration, and becomes a coding lane. The design record is [docs/plans/studio-day-one-2026-09-23.md](plans/studio-day-one-2026-09-23.md); its numbered questions are the owner's.

- [ ] **STUDIO-STAGE-01: the staging kit** (M, Sonnet). Objective: `scripts/studio/stage.sh` fetches every day-one artifact by its pinned URL and verifies its sha256 through the Stack's own download code (`stack/backend/src/lib/download.ts`), writing the Stack's store layout onto an external drive with a `STAGE.md` of every hash and size, and `--verify` re-hashes the drive; `--install <drive>` copies it into place. Items: llama-server b10797 macOS arm64, Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as GGUF at Q6 at pinned revisions, the two Splash packages (17.4 GB and 20.9 GB, pre-seeded into the Hugging Face cache layout; the package is proprietary, 4-bit weights with the vision encoder and the draft in one file that only Splash loads, so the GGUF cannot stand in for it and both forms are staged on purpose), the MLX-format weights of both candidates at pinned revisions for oMLX and mlx-serve, the pins the installer and the Stack already carry. Acceptance: `--verify` green on this Mac's drive; a dry run proves whether `splash serve` honours the pre-seeded cache with the network denied, recorded either way; the Splash formula revision in `STAGE.md` (the Studio ships with macOS 26.4, decision 1 of the record, so no macOS contingency). Out of scope: any model not in MEASURE-02. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` and `STAGE.md`.

- [ ] **STUDIO-RUNBOOK-01: the runbook, unboxing to the acceptance workload** (M, Sonnet). Objective: the record's eleven steps as a checked document (`docs/dev/studio-runbook.md`), each with its command and its check, a target under two hours; every scriptable step gains a `--dry-run` flag (`scripts/install.sh` has one) and is run on this Mac now with its output recorded. Acceptance: the dry run of every scriptable step recorded in dev.md; the restore step rehearsed against a fresh data directory from this Mac's latest backup. Out of scope: the evaluation (STUDIO-EVAL-01). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh --docs` and the recorded dry run.

- [ ] **STUDIO-EVAL-01: the Studio evaluates its own configuration** (M, Sonnet). Objective: `scripts/studio/evaluate.sh` chains, on a scratch data directory, the Stack's Studio bench protocol (`stack/scripts/bench/studio-bench.sh`), ENGINE-CONTRACT-01's suite per engine (the set is four: llama-server, oMLX, mlx-serve and Splash, each through the same suite, the same MEASURE-02 rows and the same workload; the summary picks by the numbers and the contract, never by a headline claim, and an engine that loses on chat keeps its own role: oMLX's SSD prefix cache for long companion contexts, mlx-serve's media roles), ENGINE-SPLASH-01, MEASURE-02's rows per candidate with llama-server run with the model's MTP head on and every latency measured cold and warm at 32K with the effective rate from send to last token, and STUDIO-ACCEPT-01's workload with first useful answer cold and warm, collecting the summary rows into one `report.md` in the protocol's shape and appending them to dev.md "Measured so far", so a Claude session reads tables. Mirror: `studio-bench.sh`. Acceptance: a rehearsal on this Mac (tier 1, the 8B) runs end to end and writes the report with the rehearsal marked as such; the report's summary names the candidate that passes the contract suite, clears the tool-calling bars and gives the best first useful answer under the workload. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` and the rehearsal report.

- [ ] **STUDIO-LANE-01: the Studio as a coding lane** (M, Sonnet; after STUDIO-EVAL-01). Objective: the coordinator's OpenCode HTTP driver pointed at the Studio's engine, with the lane rules from the record: a fresh session and a fresh worktree per brief at the base the coordinator names, deleted after the report; a wall-clock budget (three times a reference run) in place of a step count and a run that ends without a done report counted as blocked; the tool set the brief names (read, edit, the named tests, commit, never push); S and M coding items, second reviews by a different model, the benches. `splash claude` proven on the Studio before Claude Code is routed to it (Splash's README ships the launcher and names its Anthropic Messages endpoint; it never names Claude Code). Acceptance: one S item from the backlog done end to end on the Studio with a clean done report and a review by the other model; the driver's budget stop tested with a brief that cannot finish. Out of scope: anything the record keeps on the subscription (design, verdicts, diagnosis, cross-subsystem items, the first review of a safety change). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` and the done report.

Objective: this Mac's Home points its chat, embed and judge roles at the Studio's engines through the Stack's URL tier over the LAN (the privacy page's row unchanged: in-house); then Home moves per the runbook's step 11 with the Studio restoring from this Mac's last backup and this Mac's hub stopped, never deleted; rollback is repointing the URLs or restarting this Mac's hub on its untouched data directory. Acceptance: a turn on this Mac's hub answered by the Studio's engine; the rollback rehearsed. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh --docs` and the recorded rehearsal.

## Hardware tiers (2026-09-23)

The hub installs on what a family has; the Studio is the top of the range, not the baseline. The design is [docs/plans/hardware-tiers-2026-09-23.md](plans/hardware-tiers-2026-09-23.md): four reference points (the floor, a 24 GB Apple silicon laptop, a 16 GB CUDA laptop, a 128 GB Studio and up), one pipeline, only the budget record and the deployment limits varying, and a configuration that is proposed by the Stack's probe and stepped down by the person, never fixed. The order among voice, photos and pictures is the owner's. The Stack's own rows (STACK-SIZE-01, STACK-FLOOR-01) are in `stack/docs/BACKLOG.md`.

- [x] **VOICE-LIVE-01b: the overview route reports Home's own supervisors when no Stack is configured** (S, route + guard) - **landed 2026-09-23.** Live finding, the day VOICE-LIVE-01 landed: Jesse reloaded 8787 (no Stack) and saw no waveform button. Cause: `GET /api/engines`'s overview route returned `roles: []` unconditionally whenever `isStackConfigured()` was false (`routes/engines.ts`), so `readyRole()` (`frontend/src/apps/chat/engineRoles.ts`) could never see stt/tts as ready on a non-Stack hub no matter how healthy they really were - the same gate also silently hides `CreateImageItem` in `composerAddMenu.tsx`. Wired into the overview route's existing no-Stack branch; the Stack-configured path is untouched. Acceptance (exact words): with no Stack configured, the STT assets installed and the TTS backend startable, GET the overview lists stt and tts as ready and `/next/chat` renders the waveform button - verified with a route test using the real handlers (no mocked overview): `backend/tests/enginesRoutes.test.ts`'s two new/updated tests (the default fresh-install state, stt notInstalled/chat+tts+embed ready/image notInstalled; then with real STT asset files staged, stt ready). With the Stack configured the route's output is unchanged (existing test, untouched). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` green.

Objective: Splash (github.com/incoai/splash, Apache-2.0; Apple M3 or newer, macOS 26.4 or later, 36 GB of unified memory at least, so tier 3 only, never tier 1, tier 2 or the floor) serves exactly MEASURE-02's two Studio candidates (Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, each packaged with a DFlash 2 draft model for speculative decoding and the vision encoder) and claims about twice oMLX's decode speed on the 27B (74 tok/s short, 54 at 32K on a 48 GB M5 Pro) and close to four times under four concurrent prompts, with OpenAI Chat and Responses and Anthropic Messages endpoints, streaming, tool calls, JSON Schema output, images and reasoning_effort levels. The owner's saved transcript of a hands-on Splash review is at `data-scratch/splash/transcript-qwen38-27b-2x-faster-on-mac.txt` (git-ignored, on the dev Mac), and the session that runs this row reads it first for the claims to test. **What the review adds to this row (claims, not our record):** the baseline is llama-server at the pin with Qwen3.8-27B's own multi-token-prediction head on at draft depth two and three, never plain autoregressive decoding, because the reviewer shows Splash's 2x is its DFlash 2 draft against oMLX without one; measure cold and warm at 32K and the effective rate from send to last token (the review cites 96 s cold and 282 ms warm to first token on a 48 GB M5 Pro); include chat-shaped rows beside coding rows (the 2x was on a coding workload with reasoning on); test the 16-concurrent-32K claim against the workload's two conversations; and test Splash's refuse-to-boot memory report beside the governor's admission on the same machine, the governor staying the one authority. Nothing leans on it before it is measured: run ENGINE-CONTRACT-01's suite against it on the Studio (tool_choice required and auto, reasoning separated from content, the thinking limit, cancellation reaching the engine, timing fields), then MEASURE-02's rows and STUDIO-ACCEPT-01's workload with it beside the pinned llama-server build, recording tok/s at short, 8K and 32K context, peak memory and the concurrency result with the engine build and model digest. Files: `stack/backend/src/engineCatalog.ts` (a candidate entry, never a pin), `docs/dev.md`. Mirror: the engine catalog's existing candidate rows. Acceptance: the contract suite's pass or fail table and the numbers in dev.md; a pin only if it passes the contract and beats the pinned build on the acceptance workload. Out of scope: any code path that assumes it; the coding lane (its own decision on the Studio). Exit: the dev.md tables.

## From Open WebUI research (2026-09-24)

Why not fork Open WebUI, and what's genuinely worth taking from it: [docs/dev.md "OPENWEBUI-01"](dev.md). These three are candidates, each needs its own design pass before it is chunked further; not started.

- [ ] **CHANNELS-01: a shared, multi-person timeline** (L, design pass first). Objective: a household "family room" where more than one person shares one conversation timeline, unlike every MaiPai conversation today (one person plus the assistant). Design questions before any row is chunked: whose turn budget and content-ceiling rules apply in a multi-speaker turn, how per-person safe search resolves when the speakers differ, how the turn machine's context list handles more than one active speaker, whether a model can be addressed directly (an @-mention shape) inside it. Files: TBD, pending the design pass. Exit: TBD.
- [ ] **NOTES-01: a persistent notes workspace, attachable to chat** (M, a new catalog app). Objective: a document space separate from chat for long-form drafting, attachable to a conversation so its content injects into context, matching Open WebUI's Notes feature. Files: an assistant-ui Elements-shaped editor (no hand-built one), a hook into the existing memory/context-attach mechanism. Exit: TBD, pending a design pass on the attach mechanism.
- [ ] **STREAM-DELTA-01: measure patch-based streaming against MaiPai's own SSE** **Rewritten 2026-10-02 for chat rule 9.** Retargeted: measure the web chat's `assistant-stream` encoding (THIN-5D) against the NDJSON events on reply traffic, after THIN-5E. Verify any library claim in the installed source and cite the line, as before. (S-M, bench first). Objective: Open WebUI's v0.11.1 claims an order-of-magnitude reply-traffic reduction from patch-based rather than full-token streaming - a claim to verify in the installed source before building anything, per the org's own rule on library claims, not a number to copy. Exit: a measured comparison in dev.md; only becomes a build item if the numbers hold up.

## From DeepSeek Harness research (2026-09-26)

What DeepSeek Harness does, why it is not a base for Home, and what's worth taking: [docs/dev.md "DSH-01"](dev.md). Candidates, not started. NEXT-BRANCH-01 is a defect the audit surfaced; INCOGNITO-11 (above) is the audit's priority finding and stays in its own area.

- [x] **NEXT-BRANCH-01: an edit on `/next/chat` keeps the old reply as a branch** (S, landed 2026-09-27, `46266aca`/commons `ui-v0.5.69` `720f59b`). `/next/chat` uses assistant-ui's real `EditComposer`, not the old shell's hand-built one, so the fix needed an upstream-bound patch (same class as the Sources element's `hideTrigger`/`layout` patches): the vendored `thread.aui.tsx` gained an additive `onEditSend?: (messageId, turnId?) => void` prop, called from the edit composer's own Send click with the edited message's id and the following assistant reply's `metadata.custom.turnId`. `NextChatPage.tsx` wires it to the real `setPendingSupersedes`/`consumeSupersedes` pair `chatEditSupersedes.ts` already exports (the same module the old shell uses). Acceptance met: edit a message, reload, the BranchPicker still offers both versions (regression test). Code review clean (2 non-blocking nits). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` green, 814 tests.
- [ ] **TRACE-VIEW-01: one turn's trace, step by step, for an admin** (M, after ADMIN-LAYERS-01's panel). Objective: every turn already stores a per-node trace (`backend/src/lib/turnMachine/trace.ts`, `TurnStats.nodes` in `backend/src/wire.ts`), shown today only in aggregate on `/next/performance`; an admin opens one turn and sees each node in order with its implementation and version, outcome, start and end, the model generations with time to first token, decode time and tokens, and each tool call with its arguments and result summary, then can re-run that turn through the replay path (`backend/scripts/bench/replay.ts`'s row shape) to get a replay row. Files: a route under `/api/admin/turns/:id/trace` (zod-openapi, admin only), a `/next` page from the dashboard template's data table and chart wrapper, no hand-built UI. Acceptance: a real turn on the dev hub shows every node; a child's turn shows no reasoning text (REASONING-03 holds); non-admin gets 403; captures at 1440 and 390. Out of scope: editing or replaying with changed inputs. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.
- [x] **APPROVE-CARD-01: tap to approve a parked confirm** (S, live incident, [getmaipai/home#177](https://github.com/getmaipai/home/issues/177)). A `confirm_needed`/`consent_needed` ask now renders with assistant-ui's own approval Element (`ToolFallback.Approval`) in the thread instead of plain reply text, beside the typed or spoken "yes" that still works. **Not the kit's own `approval-card.tsx`** (design-resolver, 2026-09-27: that component is built for a terminal command - `TerminalIcon`, a monospace command box, fixed "Allow once"/"Always allow"/"Deny" labels, "Finished with exit 0" - and can't be relabeled since a shipped component is never edited). Wire shape: an additive `confirm?: { package_id: string; open: boolean }` on `TurnValue`/history rows, `open` derived at READ time against the conversation's live pending ask (a first cut baked it in permanently at write time - caught by a coordinator review before landing - so a reload kept showing an already-answered ask as still live forever); a parked ask now also gets a real `pending`/`via:"confirm"` outcome (missing on the new path before this); `POST` turn endpoints take an additive `ask_answer?: { turn_id, approved }`, matched strictly by turn id, returning `409 ask_stale` on any mismatch or missing pending ask (never a silent fallthrough that could risk confirming the wrong thing). Tapping Allow/Deny sends the same effective request a typed yes/no would, including a visible "Yes"/"No" bubble, so a live thread and a reloaded one look identical. Landed 2026-09-27: `3f692ec5` (backend: `0ed52126`, frontend: `3f692ec5`'s own commit), full gate green (backend 4304 pass, frontend 804 pass), code review clean. **The household approval queue page (M) is a separate, not-yet-started item** - `backend/src/lib/approvals.ts`/`routes/approvals.ts` exist with no frontend; re-file as its own row if picked up.
- [ ] **CONV-STATE-01: the conversation list shows which chats need you** (S). Objective: a mark on a conversation row when it is waiting on your answer (`conversations.pending_ask` set), has an unread reply, or has a scheduled routine (after ROUTINES-01). Files: the thread list adapter (`frontend/src/apps/chat/chatThreadListAdapter.ts`) and the list route's response (additive field). Acceptance: a parked ask shows the mark, answering it clears it; test in those words. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.
- [ ] **ROUTINES-01: a scheduled prompt delivered into its conversation** (M, a catalog package, design note first). Objective: "every weekday at 7, the weather and today's calendar" runs on schedule and lands in the conversation it was made in, for the person who made it, under their safety and content rules. Shape from DeepSeek Harness's schedule tools: one-shot, daily, weekly or cron with a time zone; survives restart; only the latest missed run is delivered. Built on `backend/src/lib/scheduler.ts` through the package host's `host.schedule`, never a second scheduler. Acceptance: a routine made by a child runs under the child's rules; a restart mid-schedule delivers once, not twice. Out of scope: routines that act on devices (integrations' own consent path). Exit: the design note in dev.md, then `bash scripts/check.sh`.
- [ ] **ATTACH-PREVIEW-01: preview an uploaded document beside the chat** (M, after COMPOSER-DOC-ATTACH-01). Objective: an attached PDF, office document or spreadsheet opens in the canvas side panel (`NextChatPage.tsx`'s CanvasSplit, a bottom sheet on phones). The viewer is named as a gap in the design record first: no shipped kit component renders PDF or office files today, and the smallest composition of maintained parts wins. Exit: TBD, pending that record.
- [ ] **CONV-EXPORT-01: download one conversation** (S, after EXPORT-01). Objective: a conversation's menu offers a download of that conversation alone, shaped by EXPORT-01's read-path projection (a minor gets what they can read, nothing more). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.
- [x] **SHORTCUTS-01: a keyboard shortcut reference on Cmd+/** (S, low priority). Objective: chat shortcuts (new chat, focus composer, stop reply) plus a reference sheet, from the kit's shipped dialog, listing the kit's existing Cmd+K and Cmd+B. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`. **Landed 2026-09-29 (Codex, `c49ac3a3`):** the three shortcuts wired for real, plus a Cmd+/ reference dialog listing all five entries; verified live via a real screenshot before landing.

## From Hermes research (2026-09-27)

Why Hermes Agent is not a base for Home, why the Hermes models are not a chat-role candidate, and the two things worth taking: [docs/dev.md "HERMES-01"](dev.md). Candidates, not started; each needs its own pass before it is chunked.

- [ ] **GATEWAY-01: talk to the hub from a messaging app, inbound** (L, design pass first, PRIVACY.md verdict before anything else). Objective: a family member outside the house sends a message from an app they already have (Telegram first, the channel `repairs.new` already notifies on; Signal and WhatsApp as later candidates) and gets the hub's reply back in the same chat, under their own rules. Shape from Hermes Agent's gateway: default deny, an allowlist, a one-time pairing code that binds one chat id to exactly one Person, so a child's chat runs under a child's rules and an unknown chat gets nothing. Design questions before a row is chunked: whether inbound chat through a vendor's servers is the same privacy class as the existing outbound notification toggle or a new one (the record must say, with PRIVACY.md's user-tier page updated either way); a catalog integration package (`runtime: deno`), never core; THIRD-PARTY-SERVICES.md in full. Out of scope: group chats (CHANNELS-01), voice notes. Exit: the design record in dev.md.
- [ ] **TOOL-RESULT-TRUST-01: fetched content is data, and the bench proves it** (M, research first). Objective: text the hub fetches on a person's behalf (search snippets, `read_page`, feeds, an attached document) enters the model's context with nothing marking it as untrusted and nothing measuring whether instructions inside it steer the turn; `backend/src/lib/promptSanitize.ts` only strips line breaks and braces from a display name, and `routes/llm.ts` names prompt injection in the safety list without a tool-result path. Per RULES-AND-LEARNED-COMPONENTS.md the answer is structural or measured, never a word list: a boundary the frozen turn context declares once (tool output is quoted data, an instruction inside it is never followed), a replay bench of seeded pages that carry instructions (roster-synthetic fixtures, never a real page), the pass rate recorded in dev.md, and a learned detector only if the bench shows the boundary alone is not enough, never as the sole gate in the safety path. Mirror: CORRECTION-02's one-line contract plus replay rows. Acceptance: the bench exists with its rows and numbers; a failing row is a finding to root-cause, never a patch that makes one phrasing pass. Out of scope: model-authored skills or recipes (none exist), memory poisoning (the MEM rows). Exit: the bench and its dev.md numbers, then `bash scripts/check.sh` for any code.

## From the ODS review (2026-10-01)

What ODS does, what we take, change and refuse, and why: [docs/dev/ods-review-2026-10-01.md](dev/ods-review-2026-10-01.md). Jesse's calls of 2026-10-01: the starter model is approved; the Linux image, the bill of materials and the erase action are backlogged; running the assembled Open WebUI stack as a yardstick is declined. An item that lands in another repo says so, in the way DATA-LOCATION-00d does. The first seven are next, because they get the core and its dependencies running; the rest are later.

### Next

- [ ] **SETUP-START-01: chat within minutes on a starter model** (M, Sonnet; after STACK-START-01; approved by Jesse 2026-10-01). Objective: the wizard downloads the floor profile's chat model first, opens chat, shows a banner with the full model's progress in plain words, and the swap is announced as a short pause. Files: the wizard routes and screens (`frontend/src/next/`), the banner from the template's alert as shipped. Mirror: ENGINE-AVAIL-01's derived state. Acceptance: on an empty data directory with a throttled download, a message is answered before the full model finishes; the banner names the starter and the percent; after the swap the banner is gone and a draft typed during the swap is still in the composer; a failed full download leaves chat working and raises one Repairs item. Out of scope: choosing models (SETUP-SIZE-01). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.
- [ ] **STACK-START-01: start on the floor model, swap when the chosen one lands** (M, Sonnet; lands in `getmaipai/stack`, area "Supervisor and engines"; approved by Jesse 2026-10-01). Objective: given a chosen chat model that is not yet downloaded, the Stack serves the floor profile's model, downloads the chosen one, and swaps through the existing drain and identity check, reporting each phase on the event feed. Files: `stack/backend/src/` supervisor and updates. Mirror: the update apply path's drain and rollback. Acceptance: with a throttled download a request is answered by the floor model; after the swap the chosen model answers; a failed download or failed identity check leaves the floor model serving with one health item. Out of scope: Home's banner. Exit: `scripts/check.sh` in `stack`.
- [ ] **INSTALL-PREFLIGHT-01: one preflight list for the installer and the wizard** (M, Sonnet; after DATA-LOCATION-01f). Objective: disk, memory, system version, a running instance (the lock file), a busy port and reach to the release host are returned as health-item-shaped rows with a severity and one fix, from one function the install scripts and the wizard both call. Files: `backend/src/lib/` beside `checkPlacement`, `scripts/install.sh`, `scripts/install.ps1`. Mirror: `commons/spec/schemas/health-item.schema.json`. Acceptance: each check has a fixture for pass, warning and blocker; a blocker stops the install with its fix; no check stops another program; `install.sh --check` prints the list and changes nothing. Out of scope: GPU driver installation. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.
- [ ] **INSTALL-RESUME-01: an install killed at any step finishes on the next run** (M, Sonnet). Objective: a test kills the installer after each step and proves a re-run completes, keeps the data directory, resumes a partial download and re-verifies its checksum. ## Engine availability (2026-09-29)

Design: [docs/plans/chat-engine-availability-2026-09-29.md](plans/chat-engine-availability-2026-09-29.md). Trigger: a family question got "Sorry, I couldn't do that." because an orphaned engine process held the chat port; the Repair and the notification both existed and neither reached anyone or offered a fix. Order: ENGINE-AVAIL-01 first (the state everything reads), then 02 and 03 in either order, 04, 05. Decided by Jesse 2026-09-29: Home owns its engines in its own folders, each role is single-instance behind a lock, and anything else on an engine port is reaped without asking (the note's "Decided by Jesse"). Browser push was agreed as a default channel but does not exist in Home (no subscription route, no service-worker push handler; verified 2026-09-29), so it is ENGINE-AVAIL-06 and 03 ships on in-app plus opt-in Telegram.

- [ ] **ENGINE-AVAIL-00: the composer says chat is down and stops taking messages** (S, frontend only, no backend change; the first slice, shipped alone so its effect can be seen). Objective: a signed-in person opening chat while the chat engine is down sees a kit `Alert` above the thread and a composer that is disabled with the reason in its placeholder, instead of a box that accepts a message and answers with a generic apology. Reads the existing `GET /api/health` (`engines.chat.kind` and `alive`, `requireAuth`, `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` `health()`), so it needs no new route. Pointers: `frontend/src/next/pages/NextChatPage.tsx` (the `banner` and bare-mode `Alert`s ~2683 to 2692, the `components` slots ~2809), `frontend/src/apps/chat/composerDictationWaveform.tsx` (the `ComposerInputOverride` that already renders a real `ComposerPrimitive.Input`, which takes a `disabled` prop), a new `frontend/src/apps/chat/chatAvailability.ts` for the pure kind-to-state function. Acceptance: unit tests for every `EngineHealthKind` plus `alive: false`; a component test that the input is disabled and the placeholder changes when unavailable and both revert when the engine comes back; the health query refetches (15 s, 5 s while unavailable) so the banner clears by itself; admin and non-admin copy differ per the design note; a screenshot of the real chat page opened and judged. Out of scope: any backend change, the turn engine's generic apology (ENGINE-AVAIL-02), notifications, fix buttons. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh`.
  Verified live 2026-09-29: landed on main (Codex, frontend gate green, 1,023 tests), and on the running hub with the chat port blocked the notice shows and the composer is disabled. Not covered: voice start and an already-typed draft can still send (ENGINE-AVAIL-02). New thread and its shortcut are disabled while down (ENGINE-AVAIL-00b).

## Projects (2026-09-26)

The harness design: a prompt becomes either a turn (unchanged) or a durable background project of typed recipe steps, per `docs/plans/harness-turns-and-projects-2026-09-26.md` (proposed, awaiting Jesse's read; nothing below starts before that read). The runner is Home host machinery; every project type is a catalog package shipping a recipe; hardware never branches the code, the per-model budget record and the Stack's governor do the sizing. The owner direction section (2026-09-26) sets the emphasis: the model-authored loop is the target, recipes are the skills half of the same substrate, and `plan_authoring` is gated by measurement only.

Objective: the design's project record (id, type, filled recipe, per-step state, artifacts with gate verdicts, provenance, clock stamps, terminal state) and the closed step vocabulary (`text`, `media`, `tool`, `assemble`, `gate`) as spec schemas with round-trip fixtures. Exit: commons `bash scripts/check.sh`. **Landed 2026-09-26: commons 5031401, tag spec-v0.1.40 (Codex lane from the coordinator-pinned brief; low review, zero findings, one pass; full commons gate green; the naming ruling, ProjectPlan not recipe, is in the commit message - a design-resolver pass for PROJECT-PKGTYPE-01 (2026-09-27) found this row's own claim that the ruling is also "in the design record" is wrong, corrected by that item's one-line addition to `docs/plans/harness-turns-and-projects-2026-09-26.md`).**

Objective: the tool offered per the model's budget, policy classification as consequential per the type's manifest, the starting turn's immediate reply naming the plan and duration, progress on the tool-event surface, completion posting the artifact to the thread with a notification per docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md, cancel from the thread. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` plus the flow driven end to end with a text-only recipe. **Landed 2026-09-26 (dev.md same date): `start_project` as a virtual tool (no `backend/packages/` manifest, the same shape `answer_from_this_conversation` already is), classified per a new `projectTypes.ts` registry keyed by the model's own `type` argument rather than a fixed manifest, seeded with one built-in `bedtime-story` type (text/assemble, consequential, child-available) to prove the mechanism end to end - a real catalog package retires it later (PROJECT-PACK-01). Completion posts the finished step's own text as a markdown artifact onto the STARTING turn (`createArtifact()`, keyed by `provenance.turnId` - no new `conversation_turns` row, no new `source` value) and fires new `project.done`/`project.failed` notifications; a design-resolver pass found and fixed a real race (`turnNext.ts` writes its own turn row only at the very end, so a fast-finishing project can reach "done" before that row exists) with an idempotent `postProjectResult()` called from both the runner's own terminal hook and `turnNext.ts`'s `logResult()`. Progress and cancel are `GET /api/projects/:id` and `POST /api/projects/:id/cancel` (a live per-conversation push channel is real, separate platform machinery the design never names - out of scope, named as a later item). A real, pre-existing gap found while landing: four bench scripts (`parity-bisect.ts`, `parity-bisect4-stages.ts`, `prefix-class-01-verify.ts`, `tool-calling.ts`) each build their own copy of the production tool block straight from `modelCatalog.ts`'s `tools_offered` via `loadManifestOnly()`, which cannot see a virtual tool - all four fixed to special-case `start_project` the same way `nodes/model.ts`'s own `toolSpecFor()` does, and `parityBisect4Stages.test.ts`'s own hardcoded tool count (nine, then ten) updated to match. Files: `backend/src/lib/projects/{tool,projectTypes,post}.ts`, `backend/src/lib/turnMachine/{contract,turnNext}.ts` and `nodes/{model,policy,tool}.ts`, `backend/src/lib/{modelCatalog,notificationTypes}.ts`, `backend/src/routes/projects.ts` + `app.ts`, the four bench scripts above. Out of scope, named: `media` steps (PROJECT-MEDIA-01), any real UI, a project-list-by-conversation route, a live push transport. **A medium review (one pass) found and fixed four real issues: a plan refused at validation never finalized through `postProjectResult()` at all (fixed, then a second low-effort review pass on just that fix caught the fix itself over-correcting - calling `postProjectResult()` there doubled the household's own signal for one event, an inline reply and a notification saying the same thing a moment apart, reverted to a documented no-op instead, since the refusal outcome's own `userMessage` already tells the person in the same turn); a dead `estimatedSeconds` field on `ProjectType` that nothing ever read (removed - duration always comes from the plan's own `ceilings.maxWallSeconds`); a `paramsSchema` recompiled by ajv on every single call instead of cached per type (fixed); a dead `undefined`-then-filter no-op in `post.ts`'s own sink-step lookup (fixed). The same low-effort second pass also caught `notifyResult()`'s `trigger()` calls with no `.catch()` (an unhandled rejection would have silently dropped a transient notification failure) - fixed to the same `.catch()`-and-log shape `modelDownloadJobs.ts`'s own notification calls already use. Full account in dev.md.**

Real root cause: under the household's one real catalog budget (`model_transitions: true`, `rounds: 1`), `machine.ts`'s `tool` state onDone routes ANY successful tool round - resumed or not - through one further "phrasing" round via `composer.ts`'s `phrasingInstruction()`, a prompt written for a lookup's "answer the question from the results" framing that is the wrong shape entirely for a `start_project` confirmation (the utterance was "yes"; the tool's own `result.reply.text` is already the complete thing to say). Fixed: a new `toolProvidesOwnReply` guard (`machine.ts`) checked in the same array position as `toolAllFailed` - before `moreRoundsAvailable` ever runs - routes a succeeded `start_project` outcome straight to `answer` instead, landing on `PROJECT-REPLY-01`'s own already-fixed `from_outcomes` branch. Deliberately scoped to `start_project`'s own tool id, not generalized to a "self-describing outcome" mechanism - a real open question, named not built. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` plus a `turnNext.test.ts` regression test proving zero real `model` invocations happen on the resumed turn under the household's REAL qwen3-8b budget (never forcing `NO_RECORD_BUDGET` the way `PROJECT-REPLY-01`'s own test had to), confirmed to fail without the guard and pass with it; **and** one real, live, end-to-end run (`backend/scripts/bench/project-phrase-01-live.ts`, new) against a side engine on spare ports 28788/28794 running the household's own real model, reproducing Jesse's exact scenario and reading back the actual final reply text. A medium code review caught the guard's first draft (`.some()` over the whole round) not provably matching `answerInputFrom()`'s own `.at(-1)` read - fixed to read the round's last outcome directly. A second, real but out-of-scope finding from the live run - the resumed reply's first sentence is correct but `outcomeText()`'s own pre-existing generic behavior appends `start_project`'s internal `result.data` fields (`projectId`, `stepCount`, `estimatedSeconds`) as raw text after it, now the routine case rather than a rare one - filed as [getmaipai/home#178](https://github.com/getmaipai/home/issues/178), not fixed here. **Landed 2026-09-27: full account, including the live run's own quoted reply text, in dev.md.**
- [x] **PROJECT-PACK-02: the bedtime-storybook outline names its own recurring characters** (S, live incident found the same night). Objective: a real run produced a helper character named "Starla" in chapter 2 and "Luna" in chapter 3 - a continuity slip, not a crash, because the three chapters run in parallel from the same outline (deliberate, PROJECT-PACK-01's own fan-out) and the outline step's prompt never asked the model to commit to and name a recurring character, so each chapter's own call free-invented one. Fixed: `backend/packages/bedtime-storybook/plan.json`'s `outline` step prompt now explicitly asks for "the name of any character who appears in more than one chapter" alongside the title and per-chapter lines - every chapter already reads `{{outline}}` verbatim, so naming a character once there is enough to keep every chapter consistent without touching the parallel dependency structure. Exit: one real, live, end-to-end regeneration with the same topic ("a shy dragon who's scared of the dark"), the resulting book read and the named character's own name confirmed consistent across every chapter that mentions them - a single live run is evidence of a prompt-content fix, not proof a model can never drift, and is reported as such. **Landed 2026-09-27: full account in dev.md.**
- [x] **PROJECT-REPLY-02: `outcomeText()`'s generic data-field dump excluded for `start_project`** (S, live incident, [getmaipai/home#178](https://github.com/getmaipai/home/issues/178), found while verifying `PROJECT-PHRASE-01`). Objective: a confirmed `start_project`'s reply had raw internal fields tacked on after the correct sentence ("Starting Bedtime storybook now - 5 steps, about 8 minutes. projectId: project-4o70qlua5m title: Bedtime storybook stepCount: 5 estimatedSeconds: 480."). Root cause: `answerInputFrom()`'s `from_outcomes` branch (`machine.ts`) builds the reply via `outcomeText()` (`turnContext.ts`), which after `result.reply.text` walks every scalar in `result.data` and appends it as `"key: value"` - correct for a lookup whose data fields are meant to be read, wrong for `start_project`'s `result.data` (`projectId`/`title`/`stepCount`/`estimatedSeconds`), which exists only for the frontend's tool-call consumer. Fixed: `outcomeText()` now takes `packageId` too and returns early (reply text plus `userMessage` if present, no data-field dump) when `packageId === "start_project"` - the literal string, not the `START_PROJECT_TOOL_ID` constant, to avoid a circular import (`projects/tool.ts` already imports from `turnContext.ts`). Confirmed safe for `groundOutcomes()`, `outcomeText()`'s other caller: it's only reached from the old, frozen `turnEngine.ts`, which has no `start_project` support at all. Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` (backend scope, 4300 pass) plus five new `outcomeText()` unit tests (`turnContext.test.ts`): `start_project` bare, `start_project` with `userMessage`, a non-project tool's scalar fields still flatten, `userMessage` still appends last, `rows` data still works. **Landed 2026-09-27: `ddc7f873`.**
- [x] **PROJECT-PROGRESS-01: a running project stays visibly alive in chat, no new transport** (M, live incident, [getmaipai/home#180](https://github.com/getmaipai/home/issues/180)). Objective: Jesse confirmed a bedtime-storybook project, got the "Starting X now..." reply, then total silence for ~20 seconds until the finished book appeared with no warning it was still working - he wants ChatGPT-style visible progress, not silence-then-artifact. A design-resolver pass (2026-09-27) found the right-sized v1 is polling the existing `GET /api/projects/:id` via React Query, not a new push transport (nothing to reuse - `statusChannel.ts` dies with its own turn's stream, `project.done`/`project.failed` notifications are a one-shot ping on a 15s poll, not a progress feed; the model-download job is Home's own precedent for polling a long background job, `ModelsSection.tsx:78-91`). Two blocking backend gaps found, both required before polling shows anything real: (1) `runner.ts` only saves project state once per finished BATCH, not per step - `bedtime-storybook`'s three chapters run as one parallel batch, so a poll today sees "all pending" then "all three done" with nothing in between; add a read-only `liveProject(id)` returning the running in-memory object `steps.ts` already mutates per-step, and have the GET route prefer it while the project is live. (2) the frontend never learns the project's id at all - `wire.ts`'s `TurnValue` has no `project` field (mirror the existing `artifact?` field at line ~268); add it live from the `start_project` tool outcome and on reload via a new `projectsByTurn()` lookup (mirror `artifactsByTurn()`, keyed on `provenance.turnId`, no new column). v1 progress granularity is a step counter/status line ("Writing chapter-2 (2 of 3)") built from each `StepState`'s `stepId`/`state` - no percentages or token streaming exist in the runner today, and streaming raw generated text is explicitly out (SAFETY.md: a text artifact is gated as a whole, never shown unchecked before its safety check runs). Render as the already-shipped `JobProgress` kit element (`commons/ui/src/elements/job-progress.tsx`) inside a new reserved tool-call part (`project`, mirroring how `write_document`/`tool_timeline`/`sources` already work as reserved standalone tool renders in `NextChatPage.tsx`'s `useAssistantToolUI` set) with `refetchInterval` ~2s, stopping on `done`/`failed`/`cancelled`; `onCancel` calls the existing `POST /api/projects/:id/cancel`. On finish, the live tab needs to show the posted artifact without a reload - GET response gains an optional sibling field (e.g. `posted_artifact: {id, version} | null`, looked up by the `project:<id>` tag `post.ts` already writes) so the render can show the `ArtifactCard` itself; hide it once the turn's own reload path would carry the real `artifact` field, to avoid a double card. Do NOT hold assistant-ui's own run open for the project's duration - a self-refreshing tool part is the correct shape, not a blocked composer. Files: `backend/src/lib/projects/runner.ts`, `backend/src/lib/projects/store.ts` (new `projectsByTurn()`), `backend/src/routes/projects.ts`, `backend/src/wire.ts` (`TurnValue.project`), the turn's done-value assembly for `start_project` outcomes (`turnNext.ts`/`composer.ts`), `backend/src/lib/conversationHistory.ts`, `frontend/src/lib/api.ts` (`api.project()`/`api.cancelProject()`), `frontend/src/apps/chat/{chatModelAdapter,chatHistoryAdapter}.ts`, `frontend/src/next/pages/NextChatPage.tsx`. Out of scope, named as follow-ups: PROJECT-PROGRESS-02 (each finished chapter appearing as it completes, needs a route serving one step's own gated text), an optional per-step `label` in the spec for nicer status lines, a real live push transport (only if some future feature needs genuinely sub-second continuity - this item's own poll interval is not that feature). Exit: `bash scripts/check.sh` (medium review - this changes a route shape and the wire) plus a runner test proving a mid-batch poll sees a chapter running or done (not just pending-then-all-done), a history test for the reload lookup, and a frontend render test covering polling, the stop condition, and cancel.
